children: President Donald Trump said Sunday that the United States could maintain a presence in Iran and retain control of its oil resources, comparing the possibility with Washington’s recent energy agreement in Venezuela, Reuters reported.

“We'll ultimately get out (of Iran), unless we decide to stay and keep the oil like Venezuela,” Trump said during a visit to Ireland for meetings and the Irish Open golf tournament. He claimed revenue from Venezuelan oil has “paid for the war many times.”
Trump said he still expects the Iran conflict to conclude this year, potentially after the November midterm elections. He predicted gasoline prices would “drop like a rock” once the fighting ends.

For investors, the comments add uncertainty to an already volatile energy market. Any prolonged U.S. presence in Iran could affect global oil supplies, shipping routes and geopolitical risk premiums. Meanwhile, expectations for lower gasoline prices depend heavily on restoring reliable exports from the region, particularly through the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil traders were already preparing for renewed price pressure after attacks disrupted a crucial Saudi pipeline and struck a vessel traveling through the strait. The Saudi pipeline can carry about 4 million barrels a day, making its closure a significant threat to global supply.

On possible peace negotiations, Trump said he would accept only the “right deal” and reject one that was “no good.” He also said Iran was “calling constantly” to negotiate, a claim Tehran has previously disputed, Reuters reported.

title: Trump floats keeping Iranian oil as conflict rattles energy markets
